messages.subject: multiple categorical covariate with continuous mediator
parts:
Hi there, 

I would like to check if I specified my mediation model correctly in lavaan and whether my interpretation of the results is accurate.
  • I have a categorical exogenous variable which I dummy coded (10 groups, so 1st reference group is excluded and 9 focal groups are included in the model)
  • I have a continuous mediator variable
  • I have a continuous outcome variable

# mediation model
mymodel = ' 
          impt               =~ D4  + D5  + D8 + D11 + D12 
          speed_vac     =~ D6 + D7 + D13
          works             =~ D1 + D2 + D3
          side_effects  =~ D9 + D10 + D14

          # higher order (mediator)
          beliefs =~ impt + speed_vac  + side_effects + works
          
          # hesistancy (outcome variable)
          hes =~ C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + C5 + C6 + C7
          
          # beliefs (mediator) regress on randomised condition (IV)
          beliefs ~ a1*QhidStatement2 + a2*QhidStatement3 + a3*QhidStatement4 +
                           a4*QhidStatement5 + a5*QhidStatement6 + a6*QhidStatement7 + 
                            a7*QhidStatement8 + a8*QhidStatement9 + a9*QhidStatement10
          
          # hes ~ mediator
           hes ~ b*beliefs
          
          # direct effect (hes ~ randomised condition)
          hes ~ c1*QhidStatement2 + c2*QhidStatement3 + c3*QhidStatement4 +
                     c4*QhidStatement5 + c5*QhidStatement6 + c6*QhidStatement7 + 
                     c7*QhidStatement8 + c8*QhidStatement9 + c9*QhidStatement10
          
          #indirect effect 
          a1b := a1*b
          a2b := a2*b  
          a3b := a3*b
          a4b := a4*b
          a5b := a5*b
          a6b := a6*b
          a7b := a7*b
          a8b := a8*b
          a9b := a9*b
          
          # total effect
          total := c1 + c2 + c3 + c4 + c5 + c6 + c7 + c8 + c9 + 
                   a1b + a2b + a3b + a4b + a5b + a6b + a7b + a8b + a9b
'

Under ''Defined Parameters:" it tells me that no significant mediation has taken place across all levels of QhDSttmn right? In fact, the 'regressions:' output tells me that QhdSttmn is not a significant predictor of beliefs, so there isn't even a need to run mediation in the first place. The overall effect is significant, but that is only because some of the levels in QhdSttmn (5 and 7) relative to QhdSttmn 1 is significant. In my interpretation correct?

messages.subject: Re: multiple categorical covariate with continuous mediator
parts: I would like to check if I specified my mediation model correctly in lavaan
Looks right.
no significant mediation has taken place across all levels of QhDSttmn right?
None of the individual comparisons with the reference category are significant.  If you want an omnibus test, use lavTestWald() to test the constraint that all 9 "a" paths == 0.
In fact, the 'regressions:' output tells me that QhdSttmn is not a significant predictor of beliefs, so there isn't even a need to run mediation in the first place.
Maybe the lowest negative slope is significantly different from the highest positive slope.  But if this is just post hoc fishing, you should correct for multiple (9) tests.
The overall effect is significant, but that is only because some of the levels in QhdSttmn (5 and 7) relative to QhdSttmn 1 is significant.

Probably just because you "b" path is significant.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Hi, 

I forgot I had to add in a control (nominal) variable. So I dummy coded it and used 2 of the 3 levels. (Can I assume this is an appropriate way to add in a nominal variable as controls?)
I've added the controls (pos_group and hes_group) in the mediation equation and direct effects equation as described here (https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/03gq8K324k8/m/Jt3B4apmAgAJ)
I've also simplified the code so it is easier to read. 
I assume in all results that I ignore the estimates for the control variables.

# mediation model
mymodel = ' 
          impt               =~ D4  + D5  + D8 + D11 + D12 
          speed_vac    =~ D6 + D7 + D13
          works            =~ D1 + D2 + D3
          side_effects =~ D9 + D10 + D14

          # higher order (mediator)
          beliefs =~ impt + speed_vac  + side_effects + works
# hes (outcome variable)
hes =~ C1 + C2 + C3 + C4 + C5 + C6 + C7

# m ~ x
          beliefs ~ a1*s2 + a2*s3 + a3*s4 + a4*s5 + a5*s6 +
          a6*s7 + a7*s8 + a8*s9 + a9*s10 + d1*pos_group + d2*hes_group
          
          # direct effects (y ~ m + x)
          hes ~ b*beliefs + c1*s2 + c2*s3 + c3*s4 + c4*s5 + c5*s6 +
          c6*s7 + c7*s8 + c8*s9 + c9*s10 + d3*pos_group + d4*hes_group

#indirect effect 
          a1b := a1*b
          a2b := a2*b  
          a3b := a3*b

                   a1b + a2b + a3b + a4b + a5b + a6b + a7b + a8b + a9b
'

Does the model look about right?
If some of the indirect effects are significant (e.g. a9b). Does this mean that there is a partial mediation? 

I read several papers suggesting that Baron and Kenny's approach is outdated (Woody, 2011 and Gunzler et al., 2013). So what would be the current recommended guidelines on mediation models for initial steps, specifically under the SEM framework?

Kind regards,
Aiden

Woody, E. (2011). An SEM perspective on evaluating mediation: What every clinical researcher needs to know. Journal of Experimental Psychopathology, 2(2), 210-251.

Correct, so no detectable differences from the reference category. 

how should I best correct for the multiple (9) tests in lavaan? Is it the case that I take the p-values and plug it in p.adjust()?

Yes
I dummy coded it and used 2 of the 3 levels. (Can I assume this is an appropriate way to add in a nominal variable as controls?
Yes
If some of the indirect effects are significant (e.g. a9b). Does this mean that there is a partial mediation?

If both the indirect and direct effects are significant, that is consistent with partial mediation.  If only the indirect is significant, that is consistent with full mediation.  If only the direct is significant, that is consistent with no mediation.
